messages:
darya: thinking about a small, backward-compatible tweak to make headerless safetensors streaming much safer. proposal below. :thinking:

sam: curious — what's the concrete problem you're solving?

maria: +1 to hearing it out, we've been hitting weird failures on blobstore range reads.

aj: fwiw most current bundles either have full index sidecars or we do index-first and fall back. headerless is just brittle.

darya: right. problem: for streaming (range-based) loaders we currently try to read a header up-front. headerless formats (or truncated uploads) mean we either do costly full manifest fetch or risk OOM/garbage reads. also atomic swap of in-progress uploads causes race with streaming readers.

darya: proposal: add an optional tiny 'tombstone' trailer (fixed-size footer) to safetensors bundles that encodes: magic, format-version, payload-length, and CRC. loader can do a single small tail-range request (~64 bytes) and make streaming decisions deterministically.

sam: so loader flow becomes: 1) tail-range -> see tombstone; 2a) present -> validate length+crc -> stream using range-friendly plan; 2b) absent -> fall back to index-first or manifest.

maria: that sounds nice. what's in the tombstone exactly? fixed layout?

darya: propose 64 bytes layout: 
```
0x00..0x07: "STOMB01" (8 bytes magic)
0x08..0x0F: version u64
0x10..0x17: payload length u64 (total bytes before tombstone)
0x18..0x37: sha256(payload) (32 bytes)
0x38..0x3F: reserved/flags
```
That totals 64 bytes. loader reads last 64 bytes, checks magic, then can range-read specific payload ranges confidently.

aj: how do we handle compressed bundles (gz)? tail might be weird.

darya: good catch. rule: tombstone only allowed for non-compressed object format. For compressed/opaque objects we rely on existing manifest-index flow. conversion tool can produce tombstoned uncompressed objects during ingest.

sam: cloud providers — do all S3/GS range requests guarantee tail reads for object multipart uploads? we've seen some multipart latency caveats.

maria: S3 supports range reads on completed objects. but if an object is still in a multi-part in-progress state you can get 404/416, so tombstone also tells loader "object completed and stable".

aj: does this create an extra round-trip cost for every model load? tail-range per shard could add up.

darya: yes tradeoff. but tail-range is tiny and often parallelizable across shards. alternative was index-first which often hits the catalog service anyway. we can optimize by batching tail requests for first N shards in one multi-range call or via a metadata service that caches tombstone info.

sam: migration plan? existing bundles lack tombstoned footers.

darya: phased: 1) accept both modes in loader (tombstone-aware fast path + index-first fallback). 2) new uploads/ingestion writes tombstone by default. 3) run background conversion for hot bundles (ingest workers add tombstone). 4) after N months, encourage tools to emit tombstones; keep fallback indefinitely but deprecate index-first at product level.

maria: can we atomically swap by writing ".tmp" then renaming? clients might read partial object during rename.

aj: rename semantics at object stores are not atomic across providers. but pattern we use: write object to final key with tombstone set only after upload completed; before completion put ephemeral key. tombstone indicates completed+verified.

darya: exactly. loader semantics: if tombstone present -> treat object as immutable/finished; if absent -> don't attempt streaming, go index-first or reject. that avoids racing with in-progress uploads.

infra-bot: deploy-check: please add tests for loader tail-read failures and cold-cache path.

sam: edgecases: partial tombstone (last 64 bytes truncated) — we should treat as absent, not corrupt. only treat as corrupt if magic present but checksum mismatch.

maria: security: someone could forge tombstone; but it's just a convenience for loaders. we still verify sha256 of payload before use and can require signed tombstones for private mode.

aj: how about an opt-in header flag in the safetensors header too? helps when a full parse is cheap.

darya: header flag is fine too, but the point is to enable streaming where header isn't present. tombstone lives at the tail so you don't need to fully parse or fetch the front.

sam: I like it. practical ask: can you sketch loader pseudocode?

darya: quick sketch:
```
// per-shard
tail = range_read(object_key, -64, -1)
if tail.magic == "STOMB01":
  if verify_sha(payload_length, tail.sha256):
    plan = build_stream_plan(payload_length)
    stream_ranges(plan)
  else:
    fallback_index_first()
else:
  fallback_index_first()
```

maria: nice. also add telemetry: tail_latency, tombstone_hit, tombstone_corrupt.

aj: any perf numbers? maybe 20-50ms for tail read vs 200-800ms for manifest lookup?

darya: we should bench but expectation: tail-range parallel across 8 shards ~ <100ms E2E vs manifest service cold 300-800ms.

sam: ok let's RFC this properly: include format bytes, migration assistant CLI, loader pseudocode, and a rollout checklist.

maria: +1. ack from me.

aj: +1 but add provider edgecases (gcs signed url expiry, azure block blobs).

infra-bot: created rfc: /rfc/000-safetensors-tombstone-trailer.md (draft). assigned reviewers: sam, maria, aj, darya.
